Requirement R01 (input): Input Autopilot Parameters. Fixed modalities: Touch and Keyboard. Intent: Allow the pilot to configure autopilot values (altitude, heading, speed) for engagement..

We will design this requirement in three sequential layers, all within THIS conversation: Function first, then Behaviour, then Structure. Conduct the sequence yourself — when a layer is agreed, state its final label clearly and move to the next.
- Functions: propose 2-3 genuinely distinct candidates labeled F-01.1, F-01.2, ... Distinct means each opens a different interaction goal — not the same goal reworded.
- Behaviours: one distinct interaction idea per fixed modality pathway (e.g. one Touch-only, one Keyboard-only), plus a Mixed pathway if it adds real value beyond the two. Labeled Be-01.<F>.1, Be-01.<F>.2, ... using the closed F index.
- Structures: 2-3 distinct sets of concrete HMI elements, labeled S-01.<F>.<Be>.1, ... using the closed F and Be indices.

Start with the Function candidates now (state the intent back first). The designer closes the whole requirement at the end.

**Intent restated:** R01 lets the pilot set autopilot target values (altitude, heading, speed) so the autopilot can be engaged with valid parameters. Fixed modalities: Touch and Keyboard.

Function candidates (each opens a distinct interaction goal):

**F-01.1 — Value specification**
The HMI's purpose is to let the pilot express the numeric autopilot targets (altitude, heading, speed) as concrete values the aircraft can act on. Goal: convert pilot intent into machine-usable parameter values.

**F-01.2 — Entry validity assurance**
The HMI's purpose is to guarantee that only in-range, well-formed parameter values are admitted before engagement. Goal: prevent invalid/unsafe autopilot targets from reaching the aircraft. (Distinct from F-01.1: specifying a value vs. ensuring the value is admissible.)

**F-01.3 — Parameter state legibility**
The HMI's purpose is to make the currently-set vs. pending target values unambiguous to the pilot at the moment of configuration. Goal: the pilot always knows what will be committed. (Distinct: not about entering or validating, but about the pilot's awareness of what's staged.)

**Recommendation:** F-01.1 is the core teleology of an *input* requirement — the reason R01 exists is to get target values into the system. F-01.2 and F-01.3 are real functions but arguably serve engagement/feedback requirements (R02, R03) and could be shared rather than owned by R01. Note R01's prior definition already bundles validation ("flags invalid entries"), so if you want R01 to own validity too, F-01.2 becomes co-primary.

Which function do you want to close on — F-01.1 alone, or F-01.1 + F-01.2?
